fix(formalizar-decisao): read who reacted and do not consult on settled decisions

## Why

Two failures in the same consultation, both on `formalizar-decisao`.

1. When the agent read a thread to find the answer, the read showed only the emoji and the count of a reaction. The agent named the person it expected as the one who reacted. The person who asked for the consultation then wrote to that person to confirm, and that person had done nothing.
2. The agent compared a data contract proposed by the implementer with the story and the design, and asked the product person to decide points the story had already settled. It had not opened the meeting notes that the task cites.

## What changed

- Passo 5: read who answered, agreed or reacted before naming anyone. Ask the tool for the list of who reacted, and say "I don't know who it was" when it is not available. A reaction alone is a weak signal.
- Passo 2: the sources to search now include every page the task cites. A proposal that differs from a recorded decision is not a contradiction between sources and not a question for whoever decided: point the difference out to whoever proposed it, cite the source, and ask for the adjustment. Ask the decider only what no source answers.
- A new entry in Problemas comuns, a line in Casos-limite and a line in Pegadinhas for each lesson, as the skill format asks.
- Version bumped from 0.6.0 to 0.6.2, one patch per commit.

## Impact

Only `formalizar-decisao`. No other skill, parameter or script changes.

## Validation

- `.agents/scripts/check-skill/run-check.sh` passes on the skill.
- The forbidden-terms search found nothing in the file, the commit messages or this text.
- Not validated in a real run yet. Real cases: read a thread with one reaction and name who reacted from the list; compare a proposed contract with a story that already decides the point and ask whoever proposed it to adjust.

fix(4197): staff sign-in never replays a TOTP code an earlier sign-in used

## Summary

The stage admin leg's recording-publish test flaked because the shared staff sign-in reused a TOTP code. The helper only remembered the last submitted code inside a single `signInAsAdmin` call, but consecutive tests sign the same stage staff account in. When the event-lifecycle sign-in and the recording-publish sign-in fell inside the same 30-second step, the second one submitted the code the first had already used. The server refuses a reused code (011 EARS-6), and from there the old helper hung until the 240 s timeout. The fix keeps the burnt code per factor for the whole worker, so a later sign-in waits for the next step and does not replay it.

## Root cause (evidence)

Playwright traces are off for this spec on purpose (they would capture the staff MFA), so the evidence comes from the stage `main` audit ledger (`ds_main.audit_ledger`, stage agent admin subject):

| Run (SHA) | Earlier sign-in uses a code | Recording sign-in, same 30 s step | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a65e38305 (run 45362565625) | 09:59:04.030 `auth.mfa.used` | 09:59:26.989 `auth.mfa.failure` reason `invalid` | attempt 1 timed out at 240 s on `#email` |
| 0c5fbaea1 (run 45375271601) | 10:54:39.351 `auth.mfa.used` | 10:54:58.601 `auth.mfa.failure` reason `invalid` | attempt 1 timed out at 240 s on `#email` |
| df8f5d010 (current main) | 11:49:38.034 `auth.mfa.used` | 11:49:48.938 `auth.mfa.failure` reason `invalid`, then 11:50:13 `auth.mfa.used` | passed in 50.0 s instead of ~25 s |

On the two failing SHAs the old helper waited for `/events` and that wait timed out. The helper then retried `/login` in the same context, which still held the pending authentication. The login page redirects such a session to `/mfa/challenge` without mounting the form, and the unbounded `#email` fill used up the test timeout. #4217 (df8f5d010) made that wait bounded and resumable, so current main recovers on a retry about 25 s later. The replay itself still happens there: the third row shows it. This PR removes the replay.

none

- Refs #4217 (bounded the symptom; this PR removes its cause)

## Delivery evidence

Change-tier: ship — test-only: only the shared Playwright staff sign-in helper and its unit test under `packages/e2e/` change.
Stage-B: N/A — no render surface.
Changeset: N/A — internal-only e2e helper change with no package release impact.
Behavior change: N/A — test-only change; runtime and user behavior are unchanged.
Local touched-suite verification: PASS — `pnpm --filter @ds/e2e exec vitest run` (77 files, 880 tests); `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` on `@ds/e2e`; `pnpm pr:preflight --static` (38 guards passed); all PASS.
Deviations: N/A — no ADR/spec deviations.

TDD: the new unit case `never replays the code an earlier sign-in of the same account already used` was red before the fix (`expected '013144' not to be '013144'`, the same code submitted twice in one step) and is green with it.

Live acceptance against stage slot `main` (serving df8f5d010, i.e. this branch's base), run from the workstation with `apps/admin/playwright.flows.config.ts`, `--workers=1`, the live env only, and a test list (no `--grep`):

- With the fix, the leg in its stage order (`stage-congress-review`, `stage-event-lifecycle`, `stage-recording-publish`) ran 20 times in a row, 12:15:59Z–12:42:36Z. `stage-recording-publish` passed 20/20, retry 0, 35.1–36.6 s each. `stage-event-lifecycle` passed 20/20. In that window the ledger has 40 `auth.mfa.used` and **0** `auth.mfa.failure` for the stage agent admin. The congress spec did not run: the workstation env did not carry the committee secrets. Its sign-in is a different account, so that gap does not affect this pairing.
- Before the fix, `stage-recording-publish` alone with `--repeat-each=20` passed 20/20 (~35 s apart). It never collides because each sign-in falls in a new step. That is why the failure appears only right after the 19–22 s event-lifecycle test.
- Cleanup: every run retires its own event. No non-hidden event created by these runs is left on slot `main`.

Residual (not in scope): the burnt code is per worker process. Two processes signing the same stage account in within one step can still collide, for example the Actions stage suite and an operator's local run at the same time. The admin flows tier runs `workers: 1`, so a single suite run is covered.

fix(desktop): bring the first app window to the front when the app joins the Dock

## Summary
On macOS, opening the first app window (Settings from the tray, Transcribe, Activity) moves stella from the menu bar into the Dock. Changing the activation policy deactivates the app, so the new window opened behind the app in front and only a second open brought it forward.

Joining the Dock now shows the app and brings the app window used last forward, the same routine the Dock icon's reopen uses. Leaving the Dock already handed activation back to the previously frontmost app; joining had no counterpart.

## Tests
- `rustfmt --check` clean on `app_window.rs`. The activation behaviour is AppKit's and has no unit seam; the presence bookkeeping it reads is covered by the existing `app_window` tests.

fix(library): keep track lists and rematches right after the album mbid cleanup

## What changed

A late review of #2131 found three problems it left behind. None of them is in a release yet.

- **Library-wide track list refetch.** A stored track list remembers the album `mbid` it was listed for. #2131's migration cleared `mbid` wherever it held the release group. The next scan would then treat every affected album as changed and look each one up on AurralBrainz and MusicBrainz. A new migration updates those albums so their stored list still counts as current. It only touches albums whose list was stored for the old value, so it also covers nightly installs that ran #2131's migration but haven't scanned since.
- **Rematching kept the old group's edition.** Matching an album to another release group cleared its track list but kept `trackListComplete`, `requestedRelease`, `edition`, and the links to songs with no files. Monitoring it afterwards skipped the lookup and queued the old group's recordings. A group change now drops those three fields and the old group's links to songs with no files. The next scan or monitor lists the new group, including for an album with no files yet. An album owned only because someone picked an edition stops being owned when rematched. Aurral-added and monitored albums keep their ownership.
- **Lidarr keys in `GET /api/library`.** Albums Aurral added still store `foreignArtistId`, `foreignAlbumId`, `foreignTrackId`, and `monitorNewItems` in metadata, and the Library response passed them through. They are now stripped from artist, album, and track metadata there and in queue responses. Track tags are unchanged.

## Why

The refetch breaks the rule against Library-proportional metadata calls, and the rematch bug downloads the wrong release.

Two review findings are left out on purpose:

- Passing a download job's `release_mbid` to the scanner would fill `mbid` on rescanned albums and trigger the same refetch.
- Using the release group, never the release, as a job's `albumMbid` touches about eleven call sites.

## Scope checklist

- [x] This pull request has one clear purpose
- [x] I kept unrelated fixes, refactors, formatting changes, dependency updates, and features out of this pull request
- [x] If this adds a feature, I linked the approved feature request or included the Discord context in the Why section

## Linked issue

Follow-up to #2131.

## Testing

- Each fix extends an existing test that fails on `main`:
  - The migration test checks that `getLibraryAlbumsToList` stays empty after the upgrade.
  - The rematch test checks the dropped fields and links, and that the album lists again.
  - The JSON contract test checks the Library pages for the Lidarr keys.
- `pnpm run check`, `pnpm test` (2700 passed, perf baseline unchanged) and `pnpm run test:integration` all pass.

- [ ] Minor: backward-compatible feature
- [x] Patch: backward-compatible fix
- [ ] None: documentation, CI, tests, or internal-only change
